structure.title: ABSTRACT
structure.text:
Solid electrolytes based on lithium titanium phosphate were prepared, and their phase, porosity of the sintered pellets, and electrical conductivity were studied. The conductivity was increased and the porosity decreased greatly by partially replacing  $Ti^{4+}$  and  $P^{5+}$  in  $LiTi_2(PO_4)_3$  with  $M^{3+}$  ( $M^{3+} = Al^{3+}$ ,  $Cr^{3+}$ ,  $Ga^{3+}$ ,  $Fe^{3+}$ ,  $Sc^{3+}$ ,  $In^{3+}$ ,  $Lu^{3+}$ ,  $Y^{3+}$ , and  $La^{3+}$ ) and  $Si^{4+}$  ions, respectively. The maximum conductivity at 298 K is  $7 \times 10^{-4}$  S cm<sup>-1</sup> for  $Li_{1.3}M_{0.3}Ti_{1.7}(PO_4)_3$  (M = Al and Sc). The conductivity was considerably increased by the mixing of binders such as  $Li_2O$  or  $Li_4P_2O_7$  with  $LiTi_2(PO_4)_3$ . The main reason for the conductivity enhancement of these electrolytes seems to be attributable to the increase of the sintered pellet density with the enhancement of the lithium concentration at the grain boundaries.

Recently high energy density and long life batteries using solid electrolytes have been requested. Lithium ion conductors especially are promising as the electrolyte for this purpose.

Li<sub>3</sub>N is well-known as the highest conductivity lithium conductor at room temperature (1, 2). The conductivity of glasses based on Li<sub>2</sub>S is also reasonably high (3, 4). However, these materials are not stable in an air atmosphere. A NASICON-type network structure (5, 6) is promising in its high conductivity and stability in air. The Na<sub>1+x</sub>Zr<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>P<sub>3-x</sub>O<sub>12</sub> system (NASICON) whose P<sup>5+</sup> site is partially substituted with Si<sup>4+</sup> in NaZr<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> shows a high sodium ionic conductivity. However, the Li<sub>1+x</sub>Zr<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>P<sub>3-x</sub>O<sub>12</sub> system, which is a Li analogue of the Na<sub>1+x</sub>Zr<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>P<sub>3-x</sub>O<sub>12</sub> system, exhibits a low ionic conductivity because a Li<sup>+</sup> ion is too small in size to migrate freely in their three-dimensional network structures.

The ionic conductivity for the system is greatly increased when  $\mathrm{Zr^{4+}}$  in  $\mathrm{LiZr_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}}$  is replaced by the smaller Ti<sup>4+</sup> ion (7), since tunnels in LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> are more suitable in size for the lithium ion migration. It has been already reported that the conductivity for LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> increases appreciably if Ti<sup>4+</sup> in the phosphate is partially substituted by a larger cation such as  $Ga^{3+}$  (8),  $Cr^{3+}$ (9),  $Sc^{3+}$  (7), or  $In^{3+}$ (10, 11). However, the reasons for the conductivity enhancement by the M3+ substitution are difficult to determine because of their close ionic radii. In our preceding paper (12), substitution effects of Ti<sup>4+</sup> in LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> by various ions (Al3+, Sc3+, Y3+, and La3+) on the conductivities have been discussed. Further, the reasons for the conductivity improvement by the M<sup>3+</sup> substitution are ascribed to the increase in lithium ion content and to the densification of the sample pellet adopted for the measurement.

In this paper,  $\mathrm{Li}_{1+x}\mathrm{Ti}_2\mathrm{Si}_z\mathrm{P}_{3-x}\mathrm{O}_{12}$  and  $\mathrm{Li}_{1+x}\mathrm{M}_x\mathrm{Ti}_{2-x}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$  ( $\mathrm{M}^{3+}=\mathrm{Al}^{3+},\mathrm{Cr}^{3+},\mathrm{Ga}^{3+},\mathrm{Fe}^{3+},\mathrm{Sc}^{3+},\mathrm{In}^{3+},\mathrm{Lu}^{3+},\mathrm{Y}^{3+},\mathrm{and}\,\mathrm{La}^{3+})$  systems are prepared, and their phase, ionic conductivity, and porosity are investigated.

nodes.title: Previous Research on NASICON-type Lithium Ion Conductors
nodes.text: The Na<sub>1+x</sub>Zr<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>P<sub>3-x</sub>O<sub>12</sub> system (NASICON) whose P<sup>5+</sup> site is partially substituted with Si<sup>4+</sup> in NaZr<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> shows a high sodium ionic conductivity. However, the Li<sub>1+x</sub>Zr<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>P<sub>3-x</sub>O<sub>12</sub> system, which is a Li analogue of the Na<sub>1+x</sub>Zr<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>P<sub>3-x</sub>O<sub>12</sub> system, exhibits a low ionic conductivity because a Li<sup>+</sup> ion is too small in size to migrate freely in their three-dimensional network structures. The ionic conductivity for the system is greatly increased when  $\mathrm{Zr^{4+}}$  in  $\mathrm{LiZr_{2}(PO_{4})_{3}}$  is replaced by the smaller Ti<sup>4+</sup> ion (7), since tunnels in LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> are more suitable in size for the lithium ion migration. It has been already reported that the conductivity for LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> increases appreciably if Ti<sup>4+</sup> in the phosphate is partially substituted by a larger cation such as  $Ga^{3+}$  (8),  $Cr^{3+}$ (9),  $Sc^{3+}$  (7), or  $In^{3+}$ (10, 11). However, the reasons for the conductivity enhancement by the M3+ substitution are difficult to determine because of their close ionic radii. In our preceding paper (12), substitution effects of Ti<sup>4+</sup> in LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> by various ions (Al3+, Sc3+, Y3+, and La3+) on the conductivities have been discussed. Further, the reasons for the conductivity improvement by the M<sup>3+</sup> substitution are ascribed to the increase in lithium ion content and to the densification of the sample pellet adopted for the measurement.

structure.title: Experimental
structure.text:
Materials.—A stoichiometric mixture of Li<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>, SiO<sub>2</sub>, M<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> (M = Al, Cr, Ga, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, Y, and La), TiO<sub>2</sub>, and (NH<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>HPO<sub>4</sub>, whose purities were at least reagent grade, was ground and heated in a platinum crucible at 1173 K for 2h. The resulting material was reground into fine powder using a ball mill for 6h by a wet process. The dried powder was reheated at 1173 K for 2h and then ballmilled again for

12h. The particle size of the dried powder was smaller than 1  $\mu$ m, which was determined by a centrifugal particle size analyzer (Shimadzu SA-CP3). A suitable amount of 3% PVA solution was added to the powder as a binder, and the mixture was pressed into pellets at a pressure of 1 × 108 Pa. The pellets were sintered at 1173  $\sim$  1523 K for 2h. The sintering temperature was chosen in such a way that high density (low porosity) pellets were obtained. Table I shows the sintering temperature (x=0.2-0.5) and the density of the pellets (x=0.3) for the  $\text{Li}_{1+x}M_x\text{Ti}_{2-x}(\text{PO}_4)_3$  systems. These sintered pellets were polished with 800 grade emery paper and gold was deposited by a vacuum evaporation onto both surfaces of the disk so as to obtain a good contact between the electrolyte and the electrode.

Measurements.—X-ray diffraction analysis (CuKα radiation) was conducted with a Rigaku Rotaflex with high purity Si powder (99.99%) as an internal standard. Electrical conductivity was measured by means of the complex impedance method with a Vector impedance meter 4800A and LCZ meter 4276A, 4277A from Hewlett Packard Company. The pellet was heated up to 473 K once before a measurement in order to eliminate the adsorbed water. Porosity of the sintered pellets was determined by the Archimedes' method.

The x-ray diffraction patterns of the solid electrolytes based on the LiTi2(PO4)3 prepared in this study were in agreement with that of a rhombohedral (R $\overline{3}C$ ) structure. $Li_{1+x}Ti_2Si_xP_{3-x}O_{12}$ system.—Lattice constants, conductivities at 298 K, and the porosities of the sintered pellets for the $\text{Li}_{1+x}\text{Ti}_2\text{Si}_x\text{P}_{3-x}\text{O}_{12}$ system are tabulated in Table II. The sintering of the samples was conducted at 1473 K for 2h. Lattice constants of the $\text{Li}_{1+x}\text{Ti}_2\text{Si}_x\text{P}_{3-x}\text{O}_{12}$ system for x > 0.3 could not be obtained because peaks in the x-ray patterns were not sharp enough. The cell constant for the a-axis increased slightly, indicating that the replacement of a P5+ ion with a Si4+ ion occurred. However, unknown peaks appeared in the patterns for the entire region of the $\text{Li}_{1+x}\text{Ti}_2\text{Si}_x\text{P}_{3-x}\text{O}_{12}$ system since the added $\text{Si}^{4+}$ did not always replace at the P5+ site. The porosity of the sintered pellets decreased remarkably and the conductivities were greatly enhanced with the increase of Si4+ substitution. The maximum conductivity, $3.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$ at 298 K, was obtained at x = 0.3. $Li_{1+x}M_xTi_{2-x}(PO_4)_3$ systems.—Lattice constants vs. x value for the $Li_{1+x}M_xTi_{2-x}(PO_4)_3$ systems are presented in Fig. 1. LiTi2(PO4)3 were partially substituted by Al3+, the lattice constants decreased linearly with the increase in $Al^{3+}$ up to x =0.4 because the ionic radius of Al3+ was smaller than that of $Ti^{4+}$ (Fig. 1). The single phase was formed up to x = 0.3, while an unknown phase appeared for x > 0.4 (Fig. 2). The replaceable limit for an Al3+ ion was around x = 0.4. In the substituted system for a slightly larger cation (Cr3+, Ga3+, or Fe3+) than Ti4+, the lattice constants slightly increased with the $M^{3+}$ fraction and no second phase appeared for x < 0.6. The $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ (Cr $^{3+}$ , Ga $^{3+}$ , or Fe $^{3+}$ ) ion is easy to place at the Ti $^{4+}$ site because its ionic radius is close to that of Ti4+. In the samples of the substituted systems for the larger Sc3+ or In3+, the lattice constants increased linearly with increase of x in the $\text{Li}_{1+x}M_x\text{Ti}_{2-x}$ (PO4)3 systems. A monoclinic phase formed as a second phase with the excess substitution of $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ (x > 0.3) and $In^{3+}$ (x > 0.4) ions for $Ti^{4+}$ . On the other hand, the lattice constants for $Lu^{3+}$ , $Y^{3+}$ , or $La^{3+}$ analogues were the same as that for LiTi2(PO4)3. The replacement of the Ti4+ site with $Lu^{3+}$ , $Y^{3+}$ , or $La^{3+}$ did not occur because of their larger ionic radii, and this resulted in mixed phases of LiTi2(PO4)3 and $\text{Li}_3\text{M}_2(\text{PO}_4)_3$ (M = Lu, Y, or La). The relation between the lattice constants and the ionic radius of M3+ $\mathrm{Li}_{1.3}\mathrm{M(III)}_{0.3}\mathrm{Ti}_{1.7}\mathrm{(PO_4)_3}$ (x=0.3) is presented in Fig. 3. Corresponding results for tetravalent substituted systems of $\mathrm{Li}_{1.0}\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{IV})_{0.3}\mathrm{Ti}_{1.7}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (M = Ge and Zr) were also obtained in this study and are shown in the same figure. In the samples of Al3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, Fe3+, or Sc3+ substituted systems, the lattice constants increased linearly with increasing ionic radius. The same results were also obtained for the tetravalent substituted systems. The lattice constants for the In3+ substitution deviated from the straight line in the figure, since In2O3, used as a starting material, is easily vaporized at elevated temperatures. The lattice constants for the trivalent (M = Lu, Y, or La) substituted system were equal to those for $LiTi_2(PO_4)_3$ . From these results, the $Li_{1+x}M_xTi_{2-x}(PO_4)_3$ systems are classified into two groups. - 1. Al³+, Cr³+, Ga³+, Fe³+, Sc³+, or In³+ substituted systems: $\text{Li}_{1+x}M_x\text{Ti}_{2-x}(PO_4)_3$ single phase. - 2. Lu³+, Y³+, or La³+ systems: LiTi₂(PO₄)₃ + Li₃M₂(PO₄)₃ mixed phases. The relation between the porosity of the sintered pellets and the x value for the $\mathrm{Li}_{1+x}\mathrm{M}_x\mathrm{Ti}_{2-x}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ systems is shown in Fig. 4. $\mathrm{LiTi}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (x=0) could not be obtained as a dense pellet (porosity: 34%). Porosity was decreased considerably by the $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ substitution for all systems examined. The porosity for $\mathrm{Y}^{3+}$ or $\mathrm{La}^{3+}$ mixed systems was particularly low, since the second phase formed may fill pores of the sintered $\mathrm{LiTi}_2(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ phase. On the other hand, the porosity for the $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ system is higher than that of the other systems. The po- ![](_page_2_Figure_2.jpeg) Fig. 3. The porosity tends to have a high value when the ionic radius for the $M^{3+}$ is close to that for $\operatorname{Ti}^{4+}$ . Since the ionic radius of $\operatorname{Cr}^{3+}$ is almost equal to that of $\operatorname{Ti}^{4+}$ , the porosity for the $\operatorname{Cr}^{3+}$ system is high, as is shown in Fig. 4. The sintering property is closely related to the ionic radius of the $M^{3+}$ ion. We presume that all the $M^{3+}$ ions used as a dopant do not replace the $\operatorname{Ti}^{4+}$ site completely, and a small amount of glassy second phase is formed at the grain boundaries. The quantity of the glassy phase increases in the case that the $M^{3+}$ ion does not easily replace the $\operatorname{Ti}^{4+}$ site. The $Cr^{3+}$ substituted phase might be analogous to the $LiTi_2(PO_4)_3$ single phase. Figure 6 presents the conductivity results with x in the $\mathrm{Li}_{1+x}\mathrm{M}_x\mathrm{Ti}_{2-x}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ systems at 298 K. The conductivity was greatly enhanced by the $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ substitution and the maximum conductivity was obtained at around x=0.3 for all the systems examined except for the $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ substituted one. The conductivity for the sample of $\mathrm{Li}_{1.3}\mathrm{M}_{0.3}\mathrm{Ti}_{1.7}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$ (M = Al or Sc) showed the maximum value of $7\times 10^{-4}$ S cm-1 at 298 K for all the $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ substitution systems. For the $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ , $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ , $\mathrm{Ga}^{3+}$ , $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ , $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ , or $\mathrm{In}^{3+}$ substituted system, the conductivity only not be correlated with the ionic radius of the $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ ion. In other words, the conductivity did not depend on the alteration of the cell constants by the $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$ substitution. The conductivity increased with the decrease of the porosity. In other words, the conductivity greatly depended on the density of the sintered pellets. The conductivity for the group of the mixed phase systems (Lu3+, Y3+, or La3+) was smaller than that for the single-phase ones (Al3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, Fe3+, Sc3+, or In3+). The mixed-phase systems showed high conductivity and density in comparison with single phase LiTi2(PO4)3. The second phase is influential only on the density of the pellet. The main reason for the conductivity enhancement by the $\text{M}^{3+}$ substitution is the increase of the sintered pellet density, which is very much affected by the existence of the second phase. In order to clarify the effect of high densification on the conductivity increase, a stoichiometric mixture of Li2CO3 or (NH4)2HPO4 was used as a binder for the starting materials of LiTi2(PO4)3 or Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 preparation. The binders decompose into Li2O or Li4P2O7 by the heat-treatment. Preparation for these powdered samples was the same as that for the $\text{Li}_{1+x}M_x\text{Ti}_{2-x}(\text{PO}_4)_3$ systems. All of these samples were sintered at 1173 K for 2h. The sintered samples were mixed phases [LiTi2(PO4)3 + a second phase]. However, clear peaks of a second phase were not observed from the x-ray diffraction analysis. A glassy phase might be formed in appreciable quantity by the binder utilization. Their conductivities at 298 K and the porosities are shown in Table III. The conductivity was increased and the porosity decreased greatly by the binder addition. The second-phase addition results in the increase of the lithium content, which is very effective for the enhancement of the conductivity. The lithium concentration at the grain boundaries is directly related to the lithium ion migration. The conductivity of the $Li_{1.3}Al_{0.3}Ti_{1.7}(PO_4)_3 + 0.3Li_2O$ sample is almost the same as that of the LiTi2(PO4)3 + 0.3Li2O. The Al3+ substitution for Ti4+ did not influence the conductivity increase. This result indicates that the increase of the sintered pellet density by the binder addition is the main reason for the conductivity enhancement. Table IV presents the conductivity of the bulk, the grain boundary, and the total for the samples of LiTi2(PO4)3, $\text{Li}_{1.3}\text{Al}_{0.3}\text{Ti}_{1.7}(\text{PO}_4)_3$ , and $\text{LiTi}_2(\text{PO}_4)_3 + 0.3\text{Li}_2\text{O}$ at 298 K. $\sigma_b$ , $\sigma_g$ , and $\sigma_{b+g}$ are the conductivity of the bulk, the grain boundary, and the total value, respectively. The $\sigma_b$ increased by the Al3+ substitution more than one order of magnitude in comparison with that of the LiTi2(PO4)3. However, the σb value was also enhanced by the Li2O mixing, although the second phase is only influential on the density. For all the systems, the $\sigma_{\text{b+g}}$ value is almost equal to $\sigma_g$ . This means that conduction at grain boundaries is the rate-determining step for the lithium ion migration at room temperature. Figure 9 shows the surface microstructure of the sintered pellets by a scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The LiTi2(PO4)3 sample was porous (porosity:34%) (Fig. 9a). Its particle size was around 1 $\mu$ m, which is the same as that of the starting powder. The sintered pellet of Li1.3Sc0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 was representative of the single-phase samples (porosity: 2.0%) (Fig. 9b), and the grain size is appreciably larger than that of the LiTi2(PO4)3. The pellet is easy to sinter to high density by the replacement of the Ti4+ site with M3+. In the case of the mixed phases system for Li1.3La0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3, the grains are in close contact with each other (porosity:0.1%) (Fig. 9c). Table IV. nodes.title: Analysis of Li1+xTi2SixP3-xO12 System
nodes.text:
Table II. Lattice constants (hexagonal unit), the conductivities at 298 K, and porosities of the sintered pellets for the Li<sub>1+x</sub>Ti<sub>2</sub>Si<sub>x</sub>P<sub>3-x</sub>O<sub>12</sub>

system __TBL_fc8fd37f__ network with the space group  $R\overline{3}C$ . The x-ray diffraction patterns of the solid electrolytes based on the LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> prepared in this study were in agreement with that of a rhombohedral (R $\overline{3}C$ ) structure. $Li_{1+x}Ti_2Si_xP_{3-x}O_{12}$  system.—Lattice constants, conductivities at 298 K, and the porosities of the sintered pellets for the  $\text{Li}_{1+x}\text{Ti}_2\text{Si}_x\text{P}_{3-x}\text{O}_{12}$  system are tabulated in Table II. The sintering of the samples was conducted at 1473 K for 2h. Lattice constants of the  $\text{Li}_{1+x}\text{Ti}_2\text{Si}_x\text{P}_{3-x}\text{O}_{12}$  system for x > 0.3 could not be obtained because peaks in the x-ray patterns were not sharp enough. The cell constant for the a-axis increased slightly, indicating that the replacement of a P5+ ion with a Si4+ ion occurred. However, unknown peaks appeared in the patterns for the entire region of the  $\text{Li}_{1+x}\text{Ti}_2\text{Si}_x\text{P}_{3-x}\text{O}_{12}$  system since the added  $\text{Si}^{4+}$  did not always replace at the P5+ site. The porosity of the sintered pellets decreased remarkably and the conductivities were greatly enhanced with the increase of Si4+ substitution. The maximum conductivity,  $3.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$  at 298 K, was obtained at x = 0.3.

nodes.title: Lattice Constants and Substitution Effects in Li1+xMxTi2-x(PO4)3
nodes.text:
LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> were partially substituted by Al<sup>3+</sup>, the lattice constants decreased linearly with the increase in  $Al^{3+}$  up to x =0.4 because the ionic radius of Al3+ was smaller than that of  $Ti^{4+}$  (Fig. 1). The single phase was formed up to x = 0.3, while an unknown phase appeared for x > 0.4 (Fig. 2). The replaceable limit for an Al<sup>3+</sup> ion was around x = 0.4. In the substituted system for a slightly larger cation (Cr<sup>3+</sup>, Ga<sup>3+</sup>, or Fe<sup>3+</sup>) than Ti<sup>4+</sup>, the lattice constants slightly increased with the  $M^{3+}$  fraction and no second phase appeared for x < 0.6. The  $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$  (Cr $^{3+}$ , Ga $^{3+}$ , or Fe $^{3+}$ ) ion is easy to place at the Ti $^{4+}$  site because its ionic radius is close to that of Ti4+. In the samples of the substituted systems for the larger Sc3+ or In3+, the lattice constants increased linearly with increase of x in the  $\text{Li}_{1+x}M_x\text{Ti}_{2-x}$  (PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> systems. A monoclinic phase formed as a second phase with the excess substitution of  $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$  (x > 0.3) and  $In^{3+}$  (x > 0.4) ions for  $Ti^{4+}$ . On the other hand, the lattice constants for  $Lu^{3+}$ ,  $Y^{3+}$ , or  $La^{3+}$  analogues were the same as that for LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>. The replacement of the Ti<sup>4+</sup> site with  $Lu^{3+}$ ,  $Y^{3+}$ , or  $La^{3+}$  did not occur because of their larger ionic radii, and this resulted in mixed phases of LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> and  $\text{Li}_3\text{M}_2(\text{PO}_4)_3$  (M = Lu, Y, or La). The relation between the lattice constants and the ionic radius of M3+  $\mathrm{Li}_{1.3}\mathrm{M(III)}_{0.3}\mathrm{Ti}_{1.7}\mathrm{(PO_4)_3}$  (x=0.3) is presented in Fig. 3. Corresponding results for tetravalent substituted systems of  $\mathrm{Li}_{1.0}\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{IV})_{0.3}\mathrm{Ti}_{1.7}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$  (M = Ge and Zr) were also obtained in this study and are shown in the same figure. In the samples of Al<sup>3+</sup>, Cr<sup>3+</sup>, Ga<sup>3+</sup>, Fe<sup>3+</sup>, or Sc<sup>3+</sup> substituted systems, the lattice constants increased linearly with increasing ionic radius. The same results were also obtained for the tetravalent substituted systems. The lattice constants for the In3+ substitution deviated from the straight line in the figure, since In<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, used as a starting material, is easily vaporized at elevated temperatures. The lattice constants for the trivalent (M = Lu, Y, or La) substituted system were equal to those for  $LiTi_2(PO_4)_3$ . From these results, the  $Li_{1+x}M_xTi_{2-x}(PO_4)_3$  systems are classified into two groups. - 1. Al³+, Cr³+, Ga³+, Fe³+, Sc³+, or In³+ substituted systems:  $\text{Li}_{1+x}M_x\text{Ti}_{2-x}(PO_4)_3$  single phase.
- 2. Lu³+, Y³+, or La³+ systems: LiTi₂(PO₄)₃ + Li₃M₂(PO₄)₃ mixed phases.

nodes.text:
Figure 6 presents the conductivity results with x in the  $\mathrm{Li}_{1+x}\mathrm{M}_x\mathrm{Ti}_{2-x}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$  systems at 298 K. The conductivity was greatly enhanced by the  $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$  substitution and the maximum conductivity was obtained at around x=0.3 for all the systems examined except for the  $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$  substituted one. The conductivity for the sample of  $\mathrm{Li}_{1.3}\mathrm{M}_{0.3}\mathrm{Ti}_{1.7}(\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$  (M = Al or Sc) showed the maximum value of  $7\times 10^{-4}$  S cm<sup>-1</sup> at 298 K for all the  $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$  substitution systems. In other words, the conductivity did not depend on the alteration of the cell constants by the  $\mathrm{M}^{3+}$  substitution. nodes.title: Interdependence of Conductivity, Porosity, and Second Phase
nodes.text: Figure 8 shows the relation between the conductivity at 298 K and the porosity of the sintered pellets for single phase when dopant concentrations are x=0.2 and x=0.3, and mixed phase (x=0.3, 0.4) in Fig. 2 in addition to the LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> phase. The conductivity increased with the decrease of the porosity. In other words, the conductivity greatly depended on the density of the sintered pellets. The conductivity for the group of the mixed phase systems (Lu<sup>3+</sup>, Y<sup>3+</sup>, or La<sup>3+</sup>) was smaller than that for the single-phase ones (Al<sup>3+</sup>, Cr<sup>3+</sup>, Ga<sup>3+</sup>, Fe<sup>3+</sup>, Sc<sup>3+</sup>, or In<sup>3+</sup>). The mixed-phase systems showed high conductivity and density in comparison with single phase LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>. In the mixed-phase system, the conductive phase for the lithium ion is the three-dimensional network in LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>, as the sec- __IMG_bf618fb9__ Fig. 8. The relation between the conductivity at 298 K and the porosity of the sintered pellets. The sample of the single phase  $(Li_{1+x}M_xTi_{2-x}(PO_4)_3)$  at x=0.2 ( $\triangle$ ) and x=0.3 ( $\bigcirc$ ). The sample of the mixed phase  $[LiTi_2(PO_4)_3 + Li_3M_2(PO_4)_3]$  (X). Table III. The conductivities at 298 K and the porosities for the samples using a binder __TBL_aecdb96a__ ond phase of  $\text{Li}_3\text{M}_2(PO_4)_3$  is a lower conductivity ionic conductor, which was confirmed by our measurements in this study. The second phase is influential only on the density of the pellet. The main reason for the conductivity enhancement by the  $\text{M}^{3+}$  substitution is the increase of the sintered pellet density, which is very much affected by the existence of the second phase.

nodes.title: Influence of Binders on Conductivity and Porosity
nodes.text: Table III. The conductivities at 298 K and the porosities for the samples using a binder __TBL_aecdb96a__ ond phase of  $\text{Li}_3\text{M}_2(PO_4)_3$  is a lower conductivity ionic conductor, which was confirmed by our measurements in this study. The second phase is influential only on the density of the pellet. The main reason for the conductivity enhancement by the  $\text{M}^{3+}$  substitution is the increase of the sintered pellet density, which is very much affected by the existence of the second phase. In order to clarify the effect of high densification on the conductivity increase, a stoichiometric mixture of Li<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> or (NH<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>HPO<sub>4</sub> was used as a binder for the starting materials of LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> or Li<sub>1.3</sub>Al<sub>0.3</sub>Ti<sub>1.7</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> preparation. The binders decompose into Li<sub>2</sub>O or Li<sub>4</sub>P<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> by the heat-treatment. Preparation for these powdered samples was the same as that for the  $\text{Li}_{1+x}M_x\text{Ti}_{2-x}(\text{PO}_4)_3$  systems. All of these samples were sintered at 1173 K for 2h. The sintered samples were mixed phases [LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> + a second phase]. However, clear peaks of a second phase were not observed from the x-ray diffraction analysis. A glassy phase might be formed in appreciable quantity by the binder utilization. Their conductivities at 298 K and the porosities are shown in Table III. The conductivity was increased and the porosity decreased greatly by the binder addition. The second-phase addition results in the increase of the lithium content, which is very effective for the enhancement of the conductivity. The lithium concentration at the grain boundaries is directly related to the lithium ion migration. The conductivity of the  $Li_{1.3}Al_{0.3}Ti_{1.7}(PO_4)_3 + 0.3Li_2O$ sample is almost the same as that of the LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> + 0.3Li<sub>2</sub>O. The Al<sup>3+</sup> substitution for Ti<sup>4+</sup> did not influence the conductivity increase. This result indicates that the increase of the sintered pellet density by the binder addition is the main reason for the conductivity enhancement.

nodes.title: Bulk vs. Grain Boundary Conductivity and Rate-Determining Step
nodes.text: Table IV presents the conductivity of the bulk, the grain boundary, and the total for the samples of LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>,  $\text{Li}_{1.3}\text{Al}_{0.3}\text{Ti}_{1.7}(\text{PO}_4)_3$ , and  $\text{LiTi}_2(\text{PO}_4)_3 + 0.3\text{Li}_2\text{O}$  at 298 K.  $\sigma_b$ ,  $\sigma_g$ , and  $\sigma_{b+g}$  are the conductivity of the bulk, the grain boundary, and the total value, respectively. The  $\sigma_b$  increased by the Al3+ substitution more than one order of magnitude in comparison with that of the LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>. However, the σ<sub>b</sub> value was also enhanced by the Li<sub>2</sub>O mixing, although the second phase is only influential on the density. For all the systems, the  $\sigma_{\text{b+g}}$  value is almost equal to  $\sigma_g$ . This means that conduction at grain boundaries is the rate-determining step for the lithium ion migration at room temperature. Figure 9 shows the surface microstructure of the sintered pellets by a scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> sample was porous (porosity:34%) (Fig. 9a). Its particle size was around 1  $\mu$ m, which is the same as that of the starting powder. The sintered pellet of Li<sub>1.3</sub>Sc<sub>0.3</sub>Ti<sub>1.7</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> was representative of the single-phase samples (porosity: 2.0%) (Fig. 9b), and the grain size is appreciably larger than that of the LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>. The pellet is easy to sinter to high density by the replacement of the Ti<sup>4+</sup> site with M<sup>3+</sup>. In the case of the mixed phases system for Li<sub>1.3</sub>La<sub>0.3</sub>Ti<sub>1.7</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>, the grains are in close contact with each other (porosity:0.1%) (Fig. 9c). structure.title: Conclusion
structure.text:
LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> had poor ionic conductivity and showed high porosity in the sintered pellets. The partial substitution of the P5+ site with Si4+ or of the Ti4+ site with M3+ in the LiTi<sub>2</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> system was very effective for the enhancement of the conductivity. Mixing binders such as Li<sub>2</sub>O or  $\mathrm{Li}_4 \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_7$  with  $\mathrm{Li} \mathrm{Ti}_2 (\mathrm{PO}_4)_3$  is also successful in obtaining a high conductivity lithium ionic conductor. The conductivity enhancement by the substitution or the binder addition resulted mainly from the densification of the sintered pellets. The increase of the lithium content at the grain boundaries is also effective in the conductivity enhancement.

The maximum conductivity at 298 K is  $7 \times 10^{-4} \ \mathrm{S} \ \mathrm{cm}^{-1}$ for  $\text{Li}_{1.3}\text{M}_{0.3}\text{Ti}_{1.7}(\text{PO}_4)_3$  (M = Al or Sc), which is almost equal to that of Li<sub>3</sub>N. The lithium ionic conductors based on lithium titanium phosphate are proved to be excellent solid electrolytes for their high lithium ionic conductivity even at room temperature and have a high stability in air.

Manuscript submitted March 20, 1989; revised manuscript received Sept. 23, 1989.

Osaka University assisted in meeting the publication costs of this article.
